correctness.rationale: The Gaussian core determinant is a nonzero polynomial, hence a.s. invertible. A regular nonzero isotropic point of any indefinite symmetric quadratic form has local |t|^(-p) divergence for p>=1. For arbitrary 1<=k<n, conditioning on k-1 eigenvector-near Gaussian columns preserves both signs in the Schur residual with positive probability; Tonelli gives divergence. For k=n-1, rank-one hyperplane identity and regular spherical coarea show t^-1 tail, finite moments exactly for p<1, and two-level beta law. Independent near-full matrix identities and arcsine computations corroborate.
